name: Plan site safety and file the notice of project
summary: Before work starts on a new site the general contractor, as the legal constructor, must plan how the site will be run safely and tell the ministry about the project. The safety coordinator and superintendent walk the site, write the site-specific safety plan and emergency plan, the safety manager reviews them, and the coordinator files the notice of project, posts the required documents and collects subcontractors' safety paperwork. A joint health and safety committee or a representative is arranged depending on workforce size. It is slow because site access and subcontractor documents arrive late, and error-prone because template plans are not always tailored to the site.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees with a COR-certified health and safety program and about 10 project starts a month, most of them in Ontario.
baseline.notes: Rules are Ontario's (OHSA and O. Reg. 213/91); Western and Atlantic regions follow similar provincial rules with different forms. COVID-19 site protocols were added to every plan in 2020-2022.

trigger: Operations issues the startup package for a new project.
end_state: The signed site safety plan and emergency plan are in force, the notice of project is filed and posted, and the pre-start check is passed.

volume.seasonality: Follows project starts: more from March to June.

evidence.note: Organisation file demand driver project-starts; one plan per project start.

surge.cause: spring start of the construction season

evidence.note: Follows the spring bunching of project starts; author's estimate.

systems.name: Safety management system (hazard assessments, inspections, incidents, training records)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff
Site office trailers and sea containers

steps.name: Receive the startup package and assign a coordinator
steps.description: The regional safety manager receives the startup package with the contract summary, site address, start date, logistics plan and expected trades, and assigns a site safety coordinator. Small projects share a coordinator across two or three sites.

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Determine the legal requirements for the project
steps.description: The safety manager decides which requirements apply: notice of project (expected cost over $50,000, so nearly every job), a health and safety representative or a joint health and safety committee from the expected peak workforce and duration, a worker trades committee at 50 or more workers, and any special notices for trenches, cranes or demolition.

error.defect_description: Peak workforce under-estimated, so the committee requirement is missed.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA and O. Reg. 213/91 (Construction Projects): constructor duties

steps.name: Review hazard information in the contract documents
steps.description: The safety coordinator reads the specifications, geotechnical report, existing drawings and the owner's list of designated substances (asbestos, lead, silica) and notes hazards the plan must control: excavation depth, work at height, occupied areas next to the work, overhead lines and confined spaces.

error.defect_description: A hazard in an appendix (buried tank, asbestos in a ceiling) is missed.

next.condition: designated substances report missing or out of date

evidence.note: Owners provide a designated substances list before tender on renovation work; 20% missing or outdated is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner provides the designated substances report
steps.description: The project manager asks the owner for the designated substances report or an update to it; the owner's consultant issues it, sometimes after a new survey of the existing building.

evidence.note: A new hazardous materials survey takes one to three weeks; author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive to the site
steps.description: The safety coordinator drives to the site with the superintendent once the owner gives access, taking the logistics plan, drawings and a camera.

evidence.note: Access waits on the owner's handover of the site; travel time is a typical regional trip.

steps.name: Walk the site and assess hazards
steps.description: The safety coordinator walks the site with the superintendent, checks access and egress, traffic and pedestrian routes, overhead and buried services, neighbouring occupied buildings, ground conditions and where the first aid station and muster point can go, and photographs each hazard.

error.defect_description: An overhead line near the crane radius is not recorded.

control.basis: Company health and safety program: pre-construction hazard assessment

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft the site-specific safety plan and hazard register
steps.description: The safety coordinator fills the company template: project details, roles and responsibilities, hazard register by phase with controls, fall protection, hoisting and crane rules, traffic control, excavation, PPE, site rules, subcontractor requirements, inspection schedule and orientation content.

error.defect_description: Template sections left generic, not tied to this site's hazards.

evidence.note: Contractor responsibility for safety programs (CCDC 2 GC 9.4.1) and required program content.

steps.name: Draft the emergency response plan
steps.description: The superintendent writes the emergency response plan: muster point, first aid station and first aiders, nearest hospital and route map, emergency contacts, fire and evacuation procedure, and rescue plans for falls and confined spaces.

error.defect_description: Hospital route or emergency numbers out of date.

control.basis: Written emergency procedures required on construction projects (O. Reg. 213/91)

evidence.note: A written emergency procedure must be posted.

steps.name: Review the plans against the company program
steps.description: The safety manager reads the draft safety plan and emergency plan against the corporate health and safety program and COR requirements, checks that each listed hazard has a control and a responsible person, and returns comments.

control.basis: Certificate of Recognition (COR) audit requirements for site-specific planning

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the plan and its costs
steps.description: The project manager reads the plan for cost items (hoarding, fencing, traffic control, flag persons, extra guardrails) and checks them against the general conditions budget, then signs the plan as the constructor's representative.

control.basis: Company policy: project manager signs the site-specific safety plan

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: File the notice of project
steps.description: The safety coordinator fills in the Ministry of Labour notice of project e-form in one session: constructor, owner, project address, description, estimated cost, start and end dates, peak number of workers and the first subcontractors, then prints and signs a copy.

error.defect_description: Start date or cost entered wrongly, needing an amended notice.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 s.6: constructor notifies the Ministry before construction begins on projects over $50,000

steps.name: Ministry portal confirms the notice
steps.description: The ministry's online system accepts the notice and returns a confirmation with a notice number, which the coordinator saves to the project file.

steps.name: Assemble registration forms and WSIB clearances
steps.description: The safety coordinator completes the company's registration of constructors and employers form for the project, collects the same form and current WSIB clearance certificates for the first-wave subcontractors, and files them for the site.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 registration of constructors and employers kept at the project

steps.name: Send the safety plan to the first subcontractors
steps.description: The safety coordinator emails the safety plan and site rules to the first subcontractors on site and asks for their safety program, task hazard analyses, working at heights training records and first aid certificates.

evidence.note: Working at heights and WHMIS training expected for every worker.

steps.name: Subcontractors return safety documents
steps.description: The first-wave subcontractors send back their safety programs, task hazard analyses and training records by email; small firms often send partial packages or out-of-date certificates.

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing subcontractor documents
steps.description: The safety coordinator phones and emails each subcontractor with missing training records or hazard analyses and tells them workers cannot start orientation without them.

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up first aid, fire protection and signage
steps.description: The superintendent orders and places the first aid kit and station, fire extinguishers, eye wash and site signage, names the certified first aiders on the crew, and checks the perimeter fencing and gates match the plan.

error.defect_description: First aid kit does not meet the size required for the workforce.

control.basis: First aid requirements under the Workplace Safety and Insurance Act regulation (Reg. 1101)

evidence.note: A certified first aider must be on duty; in practice done while subcontractor documents are awaited.

steps.name: Put up the health and safety board
steps.description: The safety coordinator posts the Occupational Health and Safety Act and regulations, the signed notice of project, the company health and safety and harassment policies, the emergency procedure, the ministry poster and office contact, and the names of the representative or committee members on the board in the site trailer.

control.basis: OHSA posting requirements and O. Reg. 213/91 s.6 posting of the notice of project

steps.name: Decide committee or representative
steps.description: The superintendent confirms the expected peak workforce and duration with the safety manager: 20 or more workers for more than three months needs a joint health and safety committee; six to 19 needs a health and safety representative.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA ss. 8 and 9: health and safety representatives and joint committees on construction projects

next.condition: 20 or more workers for over three months

evidence.note: Thresholds from the sources; the 55% share of projects needing a committee is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set up the joint health and safety committee
steps.description: The safety manager names the certified management member, asks the union stewards or workers to select worker members (at least one certified), sets the terms of reference and the monthly inspection and meeting schedule, and books the first meeting.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA s.9: joint health and safety committee with certified members

steps.name: Arrange selection of the health and safety representative
steps.description: The superintendent asks the workers, or the union, to select a health and safety representative once the first crews arrive and adds the name to the board.

error.defect_description: Representative not selected until after work starts.

control.basis: Ontario OHSA s.8: health and safety representative where more than five workers

steps.name: Prepare the site orientation and training matrix
steps.description: The safety coordinator builds the site orientation slides and sign-off sheet from the safety plan and sets up a training matrix listing the certificates each trade must show (working at heights, WHMIS, elevating work platforms, rigging) before working.

error.defect_description: A trade-specific certificate is left off the matrix.

steps.name: Hold the pre-start safety meeting
steps.description: The superintendent holds a pre-start meeting with the foremen of the first subcontractors and self-perform crews to go through the site rules, hazards and controls, emergency plan and orientation process.

control.basis: Company health and safety program: pre-start meeting before first work on site

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the site is ready to start safely
steps.description: The safety manager or a delegate runs the pre-start checklist: notice of project posted, emergency procedure posted, first aid and first aiders in place, fencing and signage up, committee or representative arranged, orientation ready.

control.basis: Company health and safety program: pre-start sign-off

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the pre-start gaps
steps.description: The superintendent fixes the items the checklist flagged, for example a missing posting, a fence panel or an unnamed first aider, and sends photos to the safety manager.

evidence.note: Common Ontario general contractor practice for a site-specific safety plan; durations are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Designated substances report missing
exceptions.description: Renovation or addition projects where the owner's hazardous materials report is missing or out of date; planning waits for a new survey.

exceptions.name: Plan returned by the safety manager
exceptions.description: The plan reads as a generic template or misses a hazard from the site walk and is rewritten.

exceptions.name: Subcontractor documents incomplete
exceptions.description: First-wave subcontractors send partial safety programs or training records and are chased.

exceptions.name: Pre-start gaps
exceptions.description: Postings, fencing or first aid not in place at the pre-start check.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from startup package to pre-start sign-off

evidence.note: Author's estimate: the plan and notice must be in place before construction begins, and startup packages usually reach safety three to six weeks before mobilization.

benchmarks.unit: CAD expected cost of labour and materials
benchmarks.population: Ontario construction projects (O. Reg. 213/91 s.6) during 2019-2022

evidence.note: A 2021 proposal to replace the threshold with hazard-based triggers was not in force during the period (mol_notices).

benchmarks.unit: workers regularly employed on a project expected to last more than three months

pain_points.description: Plans are copied from a template and not tailored to the site, so the safety manager returns a quarter of them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general practice.

pain_points.description: Subcontractors send safety programs and training records late or incomplete, delaying orientation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general practice.

pain_points.description: The site walk and set-up wait for the owner to hand over the site and for the trailer and fence to arrive.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Coordinators covering two or three small sites queue the paperwork behind field inspections.

evidence.note: Organisation file: 45 safety coordinators for about 220 active projects.

sources.title: Health and safety forms (Notice of Project, Registration of Constructors and Employers Engaged in Construction), archived copy
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Training and Skills Development; archived by Library and Archives Canada, 1 September 2021
sources.supports: Constructors notify the Ministry before construction begins on projects with expected total cost over $50,000 ($250,000 in an automobile factory) using Form 0175, by online e-form or paper; a signed copy is posted in a conspicuous place at the project or kept there for an inspector. Every constructor and employer completes the registration form before work begins; it is kept at the project and not submitted to the Ministry.

sources.title: Notices: proposed amendments to O. Reg. 213/91 (Construction Projects), archived copy
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Training and Skills Development; archived by Library and Archives Canada, 27 August 2021
sources.supports: 12 July 2021 proposal to modernize the Notice of Project requirement, possibly replacing the $50,000 threshold with hazard-based triggers; a proposal only during the reference period.

sources.title: Guide to the Occupational Health and Safety Act, Part II: Administration, archived copy
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Training and Skills Development; archived by Library and Archives Canada
sources.supports: A health and safety representative is required where the number of workers regularly exceeds five and no committee is required; worker trades committees are required on projects that regularly employ 50 or more workers and are expected to last at least three months.

sources.title: JHSC / Health and Safety Representative
sources.supports: Construction projects: a health and safety representative where more than 5 workers are regularly employed (6 to 19 workers on projects over three months); a JHSC instead where 20 or more workers are regularly employed and work is expected to last more than three months; at least two members under 50 workers and four at 50 or more; at least one worker and one management member must be certified.

sources.title: Getting Started (construction health and safety requirements)
sources.supports: Ministry of Labour notification for projects valued over $50,000 or meeting other O. Reg. 213/91 s.6 conditions; written health and safety policy and program where more than five employees; written emergency procedure posted; a worker with a valid first aid certificate on duty; required postings (OHSA and regulations, violence and harassment policies, ministry orders, ministry poster and office contact, names of representative or committee members); fall protection and WHMIS training.

sources.title: CCDC 2 - 2020 Stipulated Price Contract (standard form text in a District of Hudson's Hope tender package)
sources.publisher: Canadian Construction Documents Committee; document posted by the District of Hudson's Hope
sources.supports: GC 3.4.1: construction schedule submitted to owner and consultant before the first application for payment, showing major activities and critical events, monitored and updated monthly or as the Contract Documents state, consultant advised of revisions from extensions of Contract Time; GC 3.6.1: contractor makes written agreements with subcontractors and suppliers that incorporate the prime contract terms; GC 3.6.2-3.6.3: owner may object to a proposed subcontractor before signing; GC 5.2.4: schedule of values at least 15 calendar days before the first application for payment; GC 9.4.1: contractor establishes, maintains and supervises health and safety precautions and programs; GC 10.4.1: evidence of workers' compensation compliance before commencing the Work and with each application for payment; GC 11.1: contractor insurance per CCDC 41.

assumptions: Ontario rules are used because the head office and about half of the work are in Ontario. Other provinces have equivalent constructor, notice and committee rules with different thresholds and forms.

Statutes and regulations on ontario.ca and CanLII could not be opened; legal requirements are cited from the ministry's archived pages and IHSA pages (tier A only where those pages state the number). Section numbers in control bases are named for the reader and were not read in the regulation text.
The 2021 proposal to replace the $50,000 notice threshold with hazard-based triggers (mol_notices) was not in force during 2019-2022, so every project here files a notice.
The simulated median (about 30 days) is above the 25-day estimate; the benchmark is itself a tier C estimate and the gap comes from the sequential owner-access and subcontractor-document waits.
The joint committee or representative is arranged before start but often only fully formed once crews arrive; the case ends at the pre-start sign-off.
fte_on_process for each role = mean hands-on hours per case from the steps x 10 plans a month / 130 productive hours, plus 25% for calls and email not written as steps.
The org file's process links omit the safety plan going to subcontractors and to site mobilization; both are added in produces.
